sections.h2: Who sends and collects property tax in Fayette County?
sections.html:
Billing sits with the Fayette County Tax Commissioner, and valuation belongs to the Assessors' Office. The assessors issue no tax bills, and billing questions go to 770-461-3652.

The Tax Commissioner works from the county administrative complex at 140 W. Stonewall Avenue in Fayetteville. Suite 110 handles property tax and mobile homes, and Suite 109 handles motor vehicles. The mailing address is P.O. Box 70, Fayetteville, GA 30214. The property tax and mobile home counter keeps weekday hours of eight to five, and a pay-by-phone line, (770) 800-6273, takes payments.

City tax is not billed separately. All city taxes are on the county bill, and the county passes the city share to Fayetteville, Peachtree City, Tyrone, Brooks or Woolsey. For zoning or city service questions, call the city itself, for example Fayetteville at 770.461.6029 or Peachtree City at 770.487.7657.

sections.h2: The Fayette County property tax calendar
sections.html:
Statements go out in the fall, and the commissioner counts the due date as 60 days after the original mailing.

Fayette property tax timeline
EventDate or rule
Return of property valueJanuary 1 to April 1
Regular homestead applicationYear round, but complete by April 1 for that tax year
Mobile home billsMailed January 1, due on or before April 1, 10 percent penalty after the due date
Real property billsExpected around mid September
DelinquencyAfter November 15, or 60 days after mailing if that is later

Interest accrues once the bill is delinquent. A bill that never arrives does not erase the debt, so call for the balance before the delinquent date. Bills are not sent to a mortgage company unless the lender requests a copy, so give your servicer the lower portion of your bill and include the loan number.

An owner who occupies the home on January 1 can claim the regular exemption. It takes $2,000 of assessed value off the school portion and $5,000 off the county portion of the bill. Homestead is limited to one property, which must be your primary residence.

  • File any time of year, but get it complete by April 1 for the current tax year.
  • Filing can run past that date, to the end of the 45-day appeal window on the notice.
  • An approved exemption renews itself at the same address.
  • Someone who qualified for the age 62 exemption must still apply separately when reaching 65.
  • Mobile home residents are not eligible for homestead.

Both the Tax Commissioner and the Assessors' Office may handle forms, so ask which counter takes yours before you go.

Fayette voters approved House Bill 1166 in November 2020, an extra homestead exemption that applies to the school board portion of the bill. A similar measure, House Bill 581, was approved by voters in November 2024 and applies to every taxing entity except bonds. The school board opted out of HB 581 in favor of the existing HB 1166 exemption.

Both are floating exemptions, so the amount depends on the gap between the current value and a base year value. Ask the Assessors' Office which base year applies to your parcel. When you sell, buyers who ask what the property tax will be should hear that your bill reflects your own exemption status, and that they need to apply for theirs after closing.

sections.h2: How to dispute a Fayette County value
sections.html:
The appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors, postmarked inside 45 days of the date the notice was mailed. Notices for commercial and residential property have gone out in late June, and personal property notices in late July, as they did in 2026 (June 23 and July 28).

When the assessors hold their value, the case can move to the equalization board, whose records, notices and decision letters are kept by the Clerk of Superior Court. Superior Court is the next level.

Georgia also permits a written refund claim for tax charged in error, started within three years of the payment date. Filing a return between January 1 and April 1 is how an owner declares an opinion of value, and the commissioner says a return is required in the first full year of ownership and afterward only when the property changes.

Mobile home owners get their own early bill, mailed January 1 and due on or before April 1, with a 10 percent penalty after that date. Residents of a mobile home cannot claim homestead on it. If you are selling one, confirm the tax is paid and the decal is current, because the buyer will register the home with the commissioner's office and receive a new decal only after payment. For houses, no return is needed in most years once you have filed in the first full year of ownership, unless the property changes. A new addition, a pool or a sold-off lot is the sort of change that calls for a fresh return before April 1.

The county sells no tax liens or lien certificates. It runs a single real property sheriff's tax sale a year, with details on the Tax Sales tab of the commissioner's site.

A house carrying back taxes needs a written payoff from the commissioner before closing. Delinquent tax can bring penalties as well as interest, and interest begins after the delinquent date. Title companies check for open tax at closing, and a clean payoff speeds the closing.

Boats, aircraft and business personal property are taxable in whichever county holds them. A seller whose boat sits at a dock in another county gets that bill from the other county.

sections.h2: Fayette County housing at a glance
sections.html: The July 2025 estimate is 125,156 residents, up 5.0 percent from the 119,193 counted in April 2020. The county holds 47,621 housing units and 44,581 households. Because growth has been steady, buyers often ask what the bill will be, so keep recent tax statements and your exemption approval in one folder.

sections.h2: Steps to take before you sell
sections.html: Start by confirming with the Assessors' Office that your homestead and any floating exemption are on file. Next, ask the commissioner at 770-461-3652 for a written payoff good through the likely closing date, and check the delinquent date against your closing calendar. Tell your servicer about the sale so escrow is closed and refunded. In the contract, say who pays the current year, since the bill may not exist until fall. After closing, send the buyer's mailing address to the commissioner, and remind the buyer to file for homestead. A cash buyer can close faster, but the payoff and the proration still need to be settled in writing.

faqs.q: When do Fayette County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Past November 15, or 60 days after mailing if that falls later. Bills usually arrive around mid September, and interest starts once a balance is delinquent.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Fayette property tax office?
faqs.a: Dial 770-461-3652 for the Tax Commissioner, at 140 W. Stonewall Avenue, Suite 110, Fayetteville. Value questions go to the Assessors' Office, which issues no bills.

faqs.q: What is the Fayette County homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 is the standard cutoff for the current tax year. Applications can also be taken past that date, until the 45-day appeal window on the notice closes.

faqs.q: Are Fayette County mobile home taxes due on a different date?
faqs.a: Yes. Mobile home statements go out January 1 and come due by April 1, and a 10 percent penalty follows a missed date. New owners register the home with the commissioner's office and receive a decal after payment.

faqs.q: Does Fayette County sell tax liens?
faqs.a: No. Fayette sells neither tax liens nor lien certificates, and it holds one real property sheriff's tax sale a year.
